newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper editorials - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper editorials - July 21.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL urged the government to review measures monitoring the leaking of inside information on the stock market, saying there were signs of transactions behind the scenes. It said legislation and jurisdiction should be strengthened, especially now that an increasing number of mainland Chinese companies were seeking listings in Hong Kong.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said Taiwan's decision to amend the constitution was a farce, and it ignored the opinions of the public. The move was a victory for President Li Teng-hui, but a defeat to the ruling Kuomintnng party. The paper said Taiwan was a part of China, and it would remain so no matter how its system changed.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said some form of system for customs inspection involving the People's Liberation Army's Hong Kong garrison and customs officers should be put into practice. Hong Kong people needed assurance that the force was not immune from the regulations everyone else was bound by, the paper said.
